name: The Decemberists
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: [[Colin Meloy]] moved from Montana to Portland, wrote songs about sailors and ghosts, watched thieves haul off the band's gear, sent guitarist Chris Funk to duel [[Stephen Colbert]] on TV, and ended up with a number one record made in a barn.

eras.title: A pizza parlor, a silent film, a pedal steel
eras.text: Meloy left Montana and Tarkio for Portland, Oregon, took a job in a pizza parlor, and within two years had a debut out on a small local label. The name came from a failed Russian uprising of 1825; the songs came from his habit of writing about sailors, chimney sweeps and ghosts.

q: I might as well do whatever I want to do.
years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Colin Meloy · Wikipedia: Chris Funk · Wikipedia: Jenny Conlee
years.h: A pizza-parlor job in Portland turns into a band
years.p: After Missoula and Tarkio, [[Colin Meloy|c58ad99e-47ba-454b-abbe-cd72a691b46b]] meets bassist [[Nate Query|24881d66-79db-46d2-bb6f-2c3b4b1fe0c9]], who brings in keyboardist [[Jenny Conlee|c3f6819b-d2ac-468a-b75f-b6eb69d7715c]]. [[Chris Funk|19b718e1-ba75-433c-958b-918eaf522168]] turns up after a Meloy solo show.
years.xp:
Meloy paid the rent working in a pizza parlor and played open mics. Query introduced him to Conlee, who had played piano in the Portland band Calobo, and the three worked on scoring a silent film. The name comes from the Decembrist revolt, an 1825 insurrection in Imperial Russia; Meloy has said it also suited December's drama and melancholy.

Funk had met Meloy at one of his solo performances, and played pedal steel on the early records before he was officially in the band.

years.h: A McMenamins hotel gig pays for the studio
years.p: The night after playing for several hours at the hotel, the band records 5 Songs, five tracks in under two hours, and releases the EP itself.

years.cap: The band at Berbatti's Pan, Portland, October 2002
years.h: Hush Records puts out the debut, with a cover by Carson Ellis
years.p: Meloy, Funk, Conlee, Query and drummer [[Ezra Holbrook|cabce137-6afc-470c-af9d-8e0a9a31e27d]] record Castaways and Cutouts in early 2002 and produce it themselves. The cover is by [[Carson Ellis|9685d227-9744-40c4-aaa9-7ab6c17560c9]].
years.xp: Ellis, then Meloy's girlfriend and later his wife, has done the artwork for the band's releases ever since. Pitchfork gave the record 8.1.

eras.title: The label switch, a rented church, one very long song
eras.text: Signed to Kill Rock Stars, the band reissued its debut, made a first record with Rachel Blumberg on drums, and put out a single track longer than most EPs.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars takes the debut off Hush's hands
years.p: Castaways and Cutouts is reissued on May 6, 2003; Her Majesty the Decemberists and Picaresque follow on the label.

years.h: A novelist's book tour becomes a Decemberists song
years.p: Her Majesty the Decemberists, recorded February-March 2003 with producer Larry Crane, has Blumberg on drums, vibes and glockenspiel. Meloy wrote "Song for Myla Goldberg" after escorting the novelist on her Bee Season tour.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 8.2, Alternative Press five stars out of five, and Metacritic averaged 83. By November 2005 it had sold 40,000 copies in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: Colin Meloy at the Mercury Lounge, New York, March 2004
years.h: Chris Walla gets a month in a rented church
years.p: Prescott Church in northeast Portland hosts the Picaresque sessions, with [[Chris Walla|5efe021b-61c8-45ed-9c89-ab808a892c96]] producing. Accordion and hurdy-gurdy come out.
years.xp: To spark ideas, the band filled a used bike helmet with slips of paper listing strategies to try.

years.h: One 18-minute song from an Irish epic
years.p: The Tain is a single five-part track based on the myth Táin Bó Cúailnge, recorded in four days in August 2003 at Walla's Seattle studio.
years.xp: It came out first on the Spanish label Acuarela Discos in 2004 and on Kill Rock Stars in 2005, with a sleeve by Ellis. Andy Smetanka directed a video in silhouettes with minimal captions, in the manner of a silent movie, and the action runs independent of the music.

eras.title: The trailer gets stolen, Capitol calls
eras.text: The band's instruments vanished in a stolen trailer, Capitol signed it, and a sea-shanty-and-folk-tale sound found a national audience. The lineup that lasted settled in with a new drummer.

years.h: Blumberg leaves to focus on Norfolk and Western
years.p: [[John Moen|5ca14baf-075c-4bf4-8906-4d0337e11861]], who played with Stephen Malkmus's Jicks, takes the drum seat.
years.xp: Blumberg's statement said her other band needed to be her focus and the hectic schedule had made it impossible to sustain both. The announcement also named Petra Haden of That Dog as a new member. Moen was described as a cornerstone of the Portland rock community and led his own band, the Maroons.

years.cap: Meloy and the band on the Picaresque tour, 2005
years.h: Picaresque closes out the Kill Rock Stars years
years.p: The single "Sixteen Military Wives" arrives with a video distributed via BitTorrent. The record reaches No. 128 on the Billboard 200.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Chris Funk
years.h: Funk answers the stolen trailer with a banjo song
years.p: The band's equipment trailer is stolen in March 2005 and found in Clackamas, Oregon in early April, instruments gone. The banjo song is called "This Machine Kills Thieves."
years.xp: Fans bought copies of Colin Meloy Sings Morrissey on eBay and artwork by Ellis to raise money. The Shins and The Dandy Warhols helped, and C.F. Martin offered loaner guitars.

years.h: Meloy tells Pitchfork the band is going to Capitol Records
years.p: The move to a major comes after two records on Kill Rock Stars.

years.cap: The band at a daytime festival set, May 2006
years.src: Wikipedia: The Crane Wife · Wikipedia: The Decemberists
years.h: A Japanese folktale, and a major-label debut
years.p: [[Tucker Martine|3faa4491-806c-4e7f-a6a5-a9e41135d088]] and Walla co-produce The Crane Wife, built on a Japanese folktale, with cover art by Ellis. NPR listeners vote it album of the year on December 5.
years.xp: Sessions ran spring 2006. [[Laura Veirs|8951c87f-f730-4247-b442-52ed14ad6a97]] sang on it, and the band played "O Valencia!" on Late Night with Conan O'Brien the day it came out. By February 2009 it had sold about 289,000 copies in the US, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: The band at Hard Rock Live
years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Chris Funk
years.h: Colbert dodges a guitar duel and sends in Peter Frampton
years.p: After a mock feud over the band's green-screen video contest for "O Valencia!", Funk faces Colbert on The Colbert Report. Colbert feigns injury; Frampton takes his place and wins.
years.xp:
Colbert claimed his own green screen challenge came first; the band said its 2005 on-stage lightsaber fight in San Francisco predated it. The prize was a copy of The Crane Wife. Meloy has said the challenge was not scripted, though Frampton's involvement was known beforehand.

Funk afterward joined an all-guitar jam with Frampton, Robert Schneider and Rick Nielsen.

years.cap: The band at Millennium Park, Chicago, July 2007
years.h: The Los Angeles Philharmonic backs the band at the Hollywood Bowl
years.p: It is the first of five orchestral dates; Philadelphia, Atlanta and a free Chicago show with the Grant Park Symphony in August follow.

years.h: Member illness cancels the rest of the fall tour
years.p: The band calls off its remaining European dates on October 6, then on November 1 the last 28 shows of the "Long and Short of It" tour.

years.cap: Band members at the Obama rally, Portland, May 18, 2008
years.h: Barack Obama's Portland rally gets the band, one member at a time
years.p: Each member is billed individually at the rally at Tom McCall Waterfront Park.

eras.title: A rock opera, then a barn
eras.text: After a rock opera about a shape-shifter, the band went the other way: a barn, R.E.M. as a reference point, and a first number one.

years.cap: The band at Radio City Music Hall, New York, June 2009
years.src: Wikipedia: The Hazards of Love · Wikipedia: The Decemberists · The Current
years.h: The Hazards of Love is one story, played front to back
years.p: Meloy's rock opera follows Margaret and William, a shape-shifter, with [[Shara Nova|f80defee-0ef7-4238-8558-3cd6e3e76ed8]], Becky Stark and Jim James guesting. It debuts at No. 14.
years.xp:
Meloy started writing a song called "The Hazards of Love" after an Anne Briggs EP of the same name, and it grew into the album. The band played it front to back on its spring 2009 tour, and Meloy has said Stephen Sondheim's Into the Woods was a starting point. It sold about 19,000 copies in its first week.

AllMusic's James Christopher Monger called it "ambitious, pretentious, obtuse, often impenetrable, and altogether pretty great."

years.h: A bingo turner on stage picks the setlist at Terminal 5
years.p: John Wesley Harding is master of ceremonies at the Lottery Show in New York, and Veirs opens.

years.h: Every night ends with the audience eaten by a whale
years.p: On the winter European tour, the band closes with "The Mariner's Revenge Song" while the crowd screams as if swallowed and the band mimes dying.

years.src: Wikipedia: Chris Funk · Wikipedia: Jenny Conlee
years.h: Funk and Conlee start the string band [[Black Prairie|60a5cca4-c7c1-4746-b915-d39e09bbe513]]
years.p: Its first album, Feast of the Hunter's Moon, comes out on Sugar Hill Records in 2010, while the Decemberists prepare their sixth.

years.src: The Current · Wikipedia: The King Is Dead
years.h: Tucker Martine moves his studio into a hot barn for six weeks
years.p: Meloy's description of The King Is Dead, made at Pendarvis Farm near Portland. The band tried sleeping in tents on the property and gave up.
years.xp: Meloy said the goal was a shift away from British folk revival toward American music, with R.E.M. as a reference point. The barn was hot, rainy and stuffy, and he tells that part too.

years.cap: The band at Merriweather Post Pavilion, June 2011
years.src: Wikipedia: The King Is Dead · Wikipedia: The Decemberists
years.h: The King Is Dead goes straight to No. 1
years.p: [[Peter Buck|2bab20bf-8dab-4af8-b7b0-ba8e30860261]] of R.E.M. plays on three tracks, with [[Gillian Welch|2ff49515-1701-4bac-a53a-04345893f3f3]], David Rawlings and Veirs on backing vocals. It sells 94,000 copies in its first week.
years.xp: It was the band's first number one on the Billboard 200 and later went gold. "Down by the Water" was nominated for Best Rock Song at the 54th Grammy Awards, and "This Is Why We Fight" reached No. 19 on Alternative Songs.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Decemberists · Wikipedia: Jenny Conlee
years.h: Conlee is diagnosed with breast cancer
years.p: She misses tour dates during treatment; in October 2011 Meloy announces she is in remission.
years.xp: The band designed a Team Jenny t-shirt for the Yellow Bird Project, benefiting Planned Parenthood.

eras.title: The band goes quiet, then Portland names a day
eras.text: After the 2011 touring the band took a multi-year break, with a Simpsons score as its only work. A hometown return and a top-ten record followed.

years.h: The break's only job: music for a Simpsons episode
years.p: The band writes part of the score for "The Day the Earth Stood Cool." It also releases a live album and contributes "One Engine" to The Hunger Games soundtrack.

years.h: Back at the Crystal Ballroom with Castaways and Cutouts in full
years.p: Two Portland shows, the band's first in three years, each built around the 2002 debut.

years.cap: The band at the Academy of Music, Philadelphia, April 2015
years.src: Wikipedia: What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World
years.h: Portland declares Decemberists Day
years.p: Mayor Charlie Hales names January 20 for the release of What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World, the seventh album. It debuts at No. 7 on the Billboard 200 with about 50,000 copies.
years.xp:
Martine produced and mixed it. The title comes from "12/17/12," where Meloy sets his conflicted feelings about the Sandy Hook shooting against his own happy life. Guests included Kelly Hogan and Veirs.

The Boston Globe called it one of the band's "most enjoyable and lively efforts in recent memory"; Pitchfork's Jeremy D. Larson found it "overlong and under-ambitious."
play: What a Terrible World, What a Beautiful World

eras.title: Side roads, a pandemic, a new label
eras.text: The band spent these years on side roads and long looks back: a British folk record with a guest singer, a new producer, streamed anniversary shows, and in 2024 a ninth album on YABB Records.

years.h: The band teams with Olivia Chaney for Offa Rex
years.p: The Queen of Hearts, out on Nonesuch, collects traditional songs and 1970s folk-revival material sung with the British folk singer.

years.cap: The Decemberists live at Byron Bay Bluesfest
years.h: John Congleton produces I'll Be Your Girl
years.p: It is the eighth album. In August the band plays all of The Crane Wife at Prospect Park in Brooklyn, broadcast live on WFUV.

years.h: The twentieth anniversary goes online
years.p: A planned anniversary tour was pushed to 2021 and then canceled, per Pitchfork, so the band streams shows instead.

years.h: As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again lands on YABB Records
years.p: The singles "Burial Ground" and "Joan in the Garden" come first; work on the ninth album began in September 2023.
play: As It Ever Was, So It Will Be Again
